text:
maria: Quick thread — I ran a focused apples-style comparison between model-Xf16 and model-Yq4 to nail down perf deltas while holding everything else constant. Goal: confirm runtime differences are kernel/batching/kv-cache-driven, not prompt/decoding variance.

maria: Test plan summary: replay harness with identical prompt corpus (2000 short/long mix), fixed decoding params (`temp=0.0`, `top_p=0.95`, `max_new_tokens=64`, same stop sequences), tokenizer normalization enforced (vocab-normalize step applied), two cache states (cold vs warmed via prefix injection). Kernel selection pinned to `cuda-opt-v2` for both. Batching window forced to 5ms.

maria: Command I ran:```
./replay-runner --model model-Xf16 --harness prompts/2000-mix.jsonl --decoding "temp=0.0,top_p=0.95,max_new_tokens=64" --stop "\n\n" --tokenizer-normalize true --kernel cuda-opt-v2 --batch-window-ms 5 --kv-warm false --out results/x_cold.jsonl
```

maria: Then same with `--kv-warm true` and model-Yq4. identical seed in the harness: `--seed 42`.

aj: Nice. did you also force deterministic sampling on the runtime side? i.e. pin RNG at kernel boundary so outputs match exactly across runs?

maria: Yes — runtime flag `--deterministic-decode` used. We need exact token-by-token parity to exclude decoding nondeterminism.

kevin: How did you validate tokenizer alignment? small diffs in whitespace can blow up token sequences.

maria: I ran a pre-pass: canonicalize prompts with `normalize_spaces=true`, then `tokenize->detokenize` roundtrip check. For any prompt that failed the roundtrip we excluded it from the apples set (about 12/2000).

sasha: Share top-level numbers? p50/p95 latency, and token throughput?

maria: Short summary (cold cache):
- model-Xf16 p50=38ms p95=145ms tokens/s=280
- model-Yq4 p50=34ms p95=130ms tokens/s=300
- token-diff rate (exact sequence mismatch) = 0.2% (mostly trailing newline differences)

maria: Warmed cache (prefix-injected warm run):
- model-Xf16 p50=22ms p95=95ms tokens/s=520
- model-Yq4 p50=20ms p95=88ms tokens/s=560
- token-diff rate = 0.02%

aj: So quantized variant still slightly faster. Were kernels identical other than math precision? any fused-kernel fallbacks on Xf16?

maria: kernel vendor reported path `cuda-opt-v2` for both, but profiler showed Xf16 used `fused_attention_fp16` while Yq4 invoked `int8_attention_emul` + fallback for a few layer norms (adds ~0.8ms per token). We suspected that but numbers still favor Yq4 overall due to smaller memory transfers.

kevin: Interesting. Did batching heuristics spike under certain sequence lengths?

maria: Yes — with a mix >40% sequences >256 tokens we saw batching window fill slower (waiting to reach preferred batch size) => slight latency bump at p95. I re-ran with `--batch-window-ms 2` and p95 dropped ~6-8ms for long sequences but p50 regressed slightly due to less packing. There's a tradeoff.

sasha: Any evidence of KV cache thrash causing regressions on Yq4?

maria: On cold runs Yq4 showed marginally higher memcpy stalls during KV writes (observed in nvprof traces). Warm runs eliminated most of it. Suggests quantized layout causes less locality until warmed.

bench-bot: automated-summary: run_id=2026-08-03-1420, sample=2000, seed=42, deterministic=true, kernels=pinned(cuda-opt-v2), batch_window=5ms, kv_states=[cold,warm], tokenizer_normalize=true

aj: Good data. Next steps: 1) rerun with `--kernel auto` to let selector choose and capture which kernel selected per model, 2) run an apples set with longer stop sequences to stress tokenization, 3) add `--batch-window-ms 10` and 1ms to sweep.

maria: Agreed. Also want to test `--batch-scheduler=latency` vs `throughput` to see SLA impact. I'll queue the autoruns. Can someone schedule a dedicated GPU pool for the heavier sweep? (need two identical cards to avoid cross-noise).

kevin: I can reserve two p4d clones for a 3h window tomorrow morning.

sasha: I'll add a small eval to compute token-level BLEU/diff for the 0.2% mismatches to confirm they're non-semantic (whitespace/newline).

aj: One more ask — when you post the raw JSONL put the `meta.runtime_profile` snippets inline (p50/p95 per layer, kernel names) so we can feed into the perf dashboard.

maria: will do. uploading results to s3://redwood-bench/model-comparisons/2812345678/ shortly. Will ping when the auto-sweep completes. :rocket:
